theory.intro: Each neighbouring pair of mass units is linked by a factor of $1000$: tonnes to kilograms, and kilograms to grams. Convert one link at a time by multiplying or dividing by $1000$.
facts: Going to a **smaller** unit (kg→g, t→kg): **multiply** by $1000$.
Going to a **larger** unit (g→kg, kg→t): **divide** by $1000$.
steps: Identify the starting and requested units. Use $1\text{ t}=1000\text{ kg}$ and $1\text{ kg}=1000\text{ g}$.
For each link, multiply by $1000$ to use the smaller unit or divide by $1000$ to use the larger unit. Keep zeros in empty places. For tonnes and grams, use both links through kilograms.
Record the correct unit. For a mixed mass, convert its parts to the same unit and add them; for a comparison, convert all masses to the same unit before comparing.

workedExamples.question_text:
Convert to the smaller unit.
(a) $2.483$ kg to grams
(b) $3.067$ t to kilograms

Convert to the larger unit.
(a) $74$ g to kilograms
(b) $83$ kg to tonnes
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $74\div1000=0.074$.
$74\text{ g}=0.074\text{ kg}$.
(b) $83\div1000=0.083$.
$83\text{ kg}=0.083\text{ t}$.
Use zeros to hold the empty tenths places.

workedExamples.question_text:
Write each mass in grams.
(a) $2$ kg $57$ g
(b) $0.014$ t
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Convert the kilogram part, then add the grams.
$2\text{ kg}=2000\text{ g}$.
$2000+57=2057$.
The mass is $2057\text{ g}$.
(b) Convert tonnes to kilograms first.
$0.014\times1000=14$, so $0.014\text{ t}=14\text{ kg}$.
Then convert kilograms to grams.
$14\times1000=14000$.
$0.014\text{ t}=14000\text{ g}$.

workedExamples.question_text: Which is heavier: $2.036$ t or $2048$ kg? Find the difference in kilograms.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Convert to the same unit.
$2.036\times1000=2036$, so $2.036\text{ t}=2036\text{ kg}$.
$2048>2036$.
$2048-2036=12$.
The $2048\text{ kg}$ mass is heavier by $12\text{ kg}$.

development.question_text: Which is greater: $0.9\text{ t}$ or $920\text{ kg}$?
development.solution_text:
$0.9\text{ t}=900\text{ kg}$
$900\text{ kg}<920\text{ kg}$
$920\text{ kg}$ is greater.

mastery.question_text: Order $1.05\text{ t}$, $1040\text{ kg}$ and $1.004\text{ t}$ from lightest to heaviest.

A student converts $37\text{ g}$ to $0.37\text{ kg}$.
Correct the answer and explain the error.
mastery.solution_text:
$37\div1000\text{ kg}$
$=0.037\text{ kg}$
The student divided by $100$ instead of $1000$.
